implemented: Centralized Rust worker protocol/API version constants and made Rust worker requests carry an explicit worker_api_version while preserving protocol v1 request payload compatibility.

Added worker-side checks for protocol/API versions, duplicate or malformed required features, unknown required features, and unsupported state format versions. Rejections include structured codes and recovery hints before operation dispatch.
Published the worker protocol/API versions, state format versions, and required feature declarations in doctor output and docs/contracts/compatibility.json.
Added typed runtime capability descriptors to doctor output, including PyTorch and platform conditions while retaining the legacy implemented/not_implemented arrays.
Rust validates doctor capability IDs, version metadata, state format entries, and reasons for non-supported states before returning the report.
Added a Rust architecture boundary checker and a compatibility manifest consistency checker, with fixture tests proving boundary violations are rejected.

Bound required worker features and known state formats to actual Rust operation requests: model inspect/probe/loss/edit, training mode/checkpoint resume, extension inspection/conformance, environment-lock check, and supplied model variants. Caller-declared requirements are merged without repairing malformed or duplicate inputs.

Moved worker operation-to-feature declarations into a single registry used by request validation and doctor; unregistered operations and features not associated with the requested operation fail before runtime imports.

Derived doctor capability IDs from the operation registry plus the explicit host supervision feature, then applied PyTorch/platform availability conditions and per-feature providers. Compatibility checks compare the operation registry with real dispatch routes and the JSON contract.
Bound edit plans, model variants, checkpoints, extension manifests, environment-lock checks and operation features to the versions required on Rust-to-worker requests.
Added actionable rejection for unknown project-config, environment-lock and checkpoint versions. The project-config CLI test confirms an unsupported file is not overwritten.

Added exact schema_version=1 enforcement for run.json across listing, showing, mutation, cleanup and checkpoint access. Unknown run records remain untouched and include a compatible-version recovery action.
Added a Rust-owned run_record state format to the compatibility matrix and checked the documented version against the FileRunStore constant.

Human doctor output now summarizes Python/PyTorch, worker protocol/API and the same registered capability descriptors returned by --json; unknown future IDs remain visible with a readable fallback label.

integration_notes: The worker operation registry is the source for feature validation and doctor capability IDs; an AST consistency check fails when it diverges from actual dispatch routes.
Runtime conditions determine supported versus unsupported states; non-supported entries require an explanation, and Rust validates the doctor catalog before returning it.
Generic component discovery, installation and conformance reuse the existing component commands/page. This implementation added no component-specific terminal menu entries.
Unknown project config, environment lock, checkpoint, extension, variant, edit-plan or run metadata versions fail explicitly; project config and run metadata remain unchanged on rejection.
